deck.title: Warm & Fuzzies — SUEDE Designathon 2026 pitch draft
deck.narrative_rule: Move directly from the ordinary-day appreciation problem to the evidence gap, the moment of use, one solution reveal, one live demo and one team-authored handoff.
deck.evidence_rule: Every matrix position is a team hypothesis. Survey examples in the transcript are not results. Missing What, Why and How evidence remains visibly blank until documented research exists.

design.direction: Warm & Fuzzies paper-and-ink presentation system derived from Cecelia's current brand board
design.signature: An ordinary-day letter question becomes an occasion rule, a visibly unproven format gap, one live giving ritual and a real thank-you object for the room.

slides.audience_takeaway: Meet the product identity and team, then move immediately.

visual.composition: Cecelia's firefly and the Warm & Fuzzies wordmark on white, with the approved team name, team number and confirmed member names. Do not add narrative copy.

speaker_notes: Timing: 5 seconds.
Name the team and move.
Blocked until team number and member-name spelling are confirmed.

motion.description: Reveal the human-drawn identity once; no ambient loop.

slides.claim: When was the last time you genuinely sent or received a letter—outside a birthday or special event, just out of appreciation?
slides.audience_takeaway: Recall how unusual unprompted appreciation can feel before the team names the problem.

visual.composition: One full-frame question with no kicker, counterpoint, supporting sentence or raise-hands prompt.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Ask the question and pause briefly. Do not ask for raised hands.
Do not add the removed `we have never had more ways to talk` counterpoint.
Audience reflection opens the story; it is not evidence.

motion.description: One question appears once; no staged subtext.

slides.claim: We appreciate our friends and family. We just do not always show it.
slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the problem as an expression barrier, not missing care.

visual.composition: One plain problem statement in the established navy-and-white colour system. No Chloe attribution, mentor quote, persona, explanatory paragraph or orange detour.

speaker_notes: Timing: 15 seconds.
Say that appreciation can already exist while expressing it on an ordinary day still feels out of the ordinary.
Treat this as the team's current problem framing, not a prevalence finding.

motion.description: Emphasise `show it` only after the full statement lands.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the working unwritten rule and the design question it creates.

visual.composition: Birthdays, farewells and milestones each visibly supply permission; an ordinary day supplies no prompt. Close with one line: `How might we create that permission on an ordinary day?`

speaker_notes: Timing: 25 seconds.
Ask why showing appreciation appears to require a socially recognised time.
The rule is evidence-informed but its prevalence, boundaries and exceptions still require primary research.

motion.description: Show occasion prompts, then the unprompted ordinary day, then the How Might We.

slides.claim: The possible gap: meaningful enough to matter, low-friction enough to send today.
slides.audience_takeaway: See the channel hypothesis the team must test rather than accepting it as a measured opportunity.

visual.composition: A clearly labelled TEAM HYPOTHESIS map with a correct horizontal x-axis increasing left-to-right: `perceived meaning + expressive effort`; and a correct vertical y-axis increasing bottom-to-top: `practical cost: time + money + distance`. Plot quick text and voice note on the same low-cost baseline, with voice farther right. Plot video call above and farther right. Remove digital card. Swap the prior physical positions so handwritten letter occupies the former gift position and physical gift occupies the former handwritten-letter position. Highlight `THE ORDINARY-DAY GAP` without placing Warm & Fuzzies as a proven optimum. Show `___%` only as an intentionally blank result labelled `matched-format participant test pending`.

speaker_notes: Timing: 40 seconds.

Keep each comparison brief: text and voice are low-friction; video calls are synchronous; letters and gifts can feel deliberate but require more time, money or distance logistics. These are team hypotheses, not participant findings.
Point to the highlighted gap and the blank `___%`. Never insert any example number from the transcript.
The matched-format test must compare the same appreciation across text, voice or video, a physical note or gift and the prototype before the map can support an opportunity claim.

motion.description: Place the five existing channels, reveal the hypothesised gap, then reveal the deliberately blank evidence marker.

slides.claim: Before we call it a gap, we need three answers.
slides.audience_takeaway: Know the exact What, Why and How evidence that must connect the problem to the solution.

visual.composition: Three large result slots, each visibly marked PENDING. `WHAT · ___%` asks what proportion feel they have not fully expressed the appreciation they feel. `WHY · THEMES PENDING` asks what stops them, without pre-filling stigma or awkwardness as a result. `HOW · COMPARISON PENDING` rates the same appreciation formats by impact, effort and how often people would actually use them. No participant quotes, sample size or findings appear until documented research exists.

speaker_notes: Timing: 45 seconds.
Explain What, Why and How as the research structure the team reached: measure whether the problem exists, understand why, then compare how each medium performs.
Blocked until recruitment, sample, questions, method, analysis, exact results, exceptions and limitations are recorded.
The transcript's suggested 40, 100, 70 percent, 95 percent and all other example values are brainstorming, not data.
Secondary psychology and competitor evidence moves to the appendix; it cannot replace this primary evidence.

motion.description: Reveal What, Why and How in order while keeping every pending label visible.

slides.claim: When does this belong? On an ordinary day, between the moments that usually give us permission.
slides.audience_takeaway: See one complete moment of use without turning it into a market or researched persona claim.

visual.composition: A clearly labelled ILLUSTRATIVE WHEN SCENARIO: someone thinks of a person they care about on an ordinary day -> a text feels too casual, a call requires both people to be free and a physical letter will not happen today -> they choose one finite gesture -> the receiver opens it on their own time. The grandmother-granddaughter relationship may visualise the relationship, but neither person is labelled as a market segment or given invented demographic details.

speaker_notes: Timing: 30 seconds.
Answer when the experience is useful, not who might buy or adopt it.
The latest team review removed audience-segment framing from the live pitch.
This is an illustrative scenario, not validated demand or a research-derived persona. Do not invent names, ages, locations, quotes or behaviour.

motion.description: Move through the ordinary-day trigger, channel tension, finite gesture and receiver-controlled opening.

slides.audience_takeaway: Understand the proposed ordinary-day ritual in one sentence before the live demonstration.

visual.composition: Product identity, current Home state and one mechanism line only: `Make one appreciation object. Send a link. Let them open it on their own terms.` No process strip, feature inventory, future context layer, anti-doomscroll concept or impact claim.

speaker_notes: Timing: 20 seconds.
Introduce the product and switch immediately to the running prototype.
Receiving by link and without another account is the intended low-friction prototype path; production identity and delivery remain unresolved.
Call normalising appreciation a goal, not a proven outcome.

motion.description: Reveal the product name and one mechanism line, then stop deck motion for the live demo.

slides.claim: Make. Seal. Choose how it travels. Give. Open.
slides.audience_takeaway: Watch one complete working sender-to-receiver journey rather than a narrated feature tour.

visual.composition: A sparse live-demo holding slide with the five verbs and a clear cue to switch to the running prototype. Do not show separate sender, receiver or process screenshot slides and do not run a product video as well. Static captures belong only in the appendix or emergency fallback.

speaker_notes: Timing: 105 seconds.
Switch to the live prototype. Show only the critical path: compose one object, seal it, choose its travel, create the link, open as receiver, then keep, close or remove without replying.
Narrate verbs, not tools, materials or animations.
Demonstrate only working states. Do not claim delivery infrastructure, verified identity, encrypted privacy, ownership, permanent storage or lower awkwardness.
Use a preloaded static or local fallback only if the live path fails; never spend pitch time showing both a video and the live demo.

motion.description: Deck motion stops while the presenter demonstrates the working prototype; return only after the receiver outcome is visible.

slides.claim: We made something for you, too.
slides.audience_takeaway: Receive a real team-authored thank-you through the same flow, voluntarily and without reply pressure.

visual.composition: The final handoff uses a real approved photo or selfie of the team making the object, a real thank-you object with contributions from the team, and the verified live QR and URL. Include an equally clear no-device fallback. Do not ship a generic placeholder card as the final state.

speaker_notes: Timing: 35 seconds.
Thank the hosts and room, say the team made this object for them, and invite them to open it privately and optionally. No reply is expected.
Blocked until the real team photo has consent, the team-authored object is complete, the deployed receiver URL is tested on a second device, and the QR is verified at presentation distance.
A scan, smile, applause or emotional reaction demonstrates the handoff only; it is not impact evidence.

motion.description: Reveal the real team photo, then the verified handoff card. No separate conclusion slide follows.
